prompt:
TESSERA STYLE SHEET
1. Modern editorial paper collage: bold magazine composition, refined 2D motion design, photographed flat under soft room light.
2. One flat block-colour paper ground fills the frame: lime green. The ground is a single unbroken colour.
3. Subjects are black-and-white halftone photographic cutouts with rough white torn-paper edges: objects, machines, buildings, maps, coins, screens, vehicles, anonymous paper hands. Every cutout is a plain, unmarked object: calendar pages, documents, coins, screens and vehicles are blank and unprinted, with no lettering, numerals, symbols, liveries or marks on them. Every cutout is matte paper reflecting only the room light, with a plain blank face: coin rims, document faces, screens and vehicle sides carry no lettering, numerals or marks.
4. Diagram elements are flat matte paper shapes and ribbons, tape, rubber stamps, string and pins, stencilled arrows, paper bar charts, stacked sheets, grid paper, torn strips, hole-punched tags, paper clips, in cream, black, pale yellow or the ground's contrasting colour, with real paper texture and print dots.
5. One consistent light from the upper left; each paper layer casts a small soft shadow.
6. Layout: the headline chip owns the upper third of the frame and stays uncovered; subjects and diagrams occupy the lower two-thirds. When the frame opens on a previous composition, its elements slide off or are covered in the first second and the new headline lands on clear ground.
7. Headline typography: one extra-bold sans-serif in black or cream, printed on a cream or black paper chip: one line, no wider than a third of the frame width, with safe margins, the chip sitting clear of the subjects. Letterforms are accurate, complete and stable from the frame they appear in; the chip is printed once and does not redraw. When the beat marks a hero number, that number alone may be printed larger, up to half the frame width.
8. Compositions vary in scale from beat to beat: some show one oversized subject filling the frame, some a small subject alone on open ground, some several elements arranged as a diagram.
9. Motion: elements enter fast with slight overshoot and a stable landing, then hold a clear reading window; one strongest focus at a time; the camera is locked; movement starts on the first frame and a small loop continues at the end; no empty frames.
10. 16:9, exactly 5 seconds, one composition, at most one crisp cut.
11. Identity anchor: rough white torn edges on every cutout; small paper shadow from the upper-left light.

BEAT
Ground: lime green.
Subjects: a paper map; a stencilled arrow.
Opens on the single coin, carried over from the previous shot, which transforms as the action begins.
Action: The previous chip flips away as the single coin widens into a paper map; a stencilled arrow lands across it.
Ends holding on the stencilled arrow.
This composition is a diagram: several elements are arranged together.
Headline printed on a paper chip: "BRAZIL $77B".

ON-SCREEN TEXT: "BRAZIL $77B". This string is printed complete and correct from its first visible frame and never changes. It is the only lettering in the frame.

AUDIO: One English narrator, warm, clear, natural, brisk but unhurried, never an advertising shout. Speak the following line exactly once, word for word, beginning on the first frame: "Diginex has signalled focus on Brazil's seventy-seven billion dollar market.". No other dialogue. Light paper-slap and tape sound effects beneath the voice; no music.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] This is a modern editorial paper collage style, photographed as a flat lay under soft, consistent room light coming from the upper left. <Picture 1> establishes the initial scene: a lime green, flat block-color paper ground filling the frame. In the upper third, a cream paper chip with the black text "~$34M CAP" is visible. In the lower two-thirds, a black-and-white halftone photographic cutout of a coin rests on a piece of torn grid paper, both featuring rough white torn-paper edges and casting small, soft shadows. 

Immediately upon the first frame, the camera remains in a Static Shot. The cream paper chip with "~$34M CAP" flips away rapidly with a slight overshoot, replaced instantly by a new cream paper chip appearing in the upper third. This new chip features the clean, stable, extra-bold black sans-serif text "BRAZIL $77B", which remains legible and unchanged for the duration. Simultaneously, the coin cutout in the center expands and widens, transforming through a refined 2D motion design into a large, black-and-white halftone photographic cutout of a paper map. The map is unmarked and plain, with the same rough white torn edges and matte paper texture. Shortly after the map lands, a flat matte paper stencilled arrow in a contrasting black color slides in quickly and lands decisively across the map. The arrow and map hold a clear reading window, with the composition forming a diagram. The video ends with a small, subtle loop of the elements shifting slightly.

overall_soundscape: A sequence of crisp, tactile paper-slap sounds as the chip flips and the map expands, followed by the sharp, sticky sound of tape being pressed down as the stencilled arrow lands on the paper ground.
